implementation_plan.title: Struct creation and destruction
implementation_plan.goal: InversionList::new constructs from (capacity, values), coalescing sorted/deduplicated values into intervals; validates value < capacity; Drop is automatic.
steps_part_a: Implement InversionList::new: sort a local Vec<u32> copy of values, validate each value < capacity else Err(ValueOutOfRange(value, capacity)), coalesce adjacent/duplicate sorted values into (start,end) intervals, compute support as distinct value count, return Ok(Self { capacity, support, intervals }).
steps_part_b: Remove #[ignore] from test_struct: construct a small set, assert capacity/support/intervals fields make sense (via accessors) for a simple contiguous input.
Remove #[ignore] from test_create_destroy_2: construct and drop a set with multiple disjoint values; assert no panic and correct intervals via public accessors.

implementation_plan.title: Getters and creation edge cases
implementation_plan.goal: capacity()/support() return correct values; new() handles empty values, values == capacity-1 boundary, out-of-range values, and duplicate/unsorted input.
steps_part_a: Implement InversionList::capacity as self.capacity.
Implement InversionList::support as self.support.

Confirm InversionList::new (M1) already handles: empty values slice -> support 0, empty intervals; unsorted/duplicate input -> sorted+deduped coalescing; any value >= capacity -> Err(ValueOutOfRange(value, capacity)) using the first offending value found.
steps_part_b: Remove #[ignore] from test_getters: assert capacity()/support() on sets built with known capacities/values.

Remove #[ignore] from test_create_destroy_4: assert unsorted/duplicate values coalesce correctly and out-of-range values yield Err(ValueOutOfRange(..)).

steps_part_a: Implement InversionList::contains(value): scan/binary-search self.intervals for an interval (lo,hi) with lo <= value < hi; return bool.
steps_part_b: Remove #[ignore] from test_member: assert contains() true/false for interior, exterior, and exact boundary (start and end) values on a multi-interval set.

steps_part_a: Implement InversionList::to_str: expand every interval into individual member values in order, join with ', ', wrap in '[' ']'.
Implement impl fmt::Display for InversionList::fmt to delegate to to_str (or equivalent shared logic).
steps_part_b: Remove #[ignore] from test_to_string: assert to_str() on an empty set is '[]', and on a known multi-interval set matches the expected expanded string; assert Display (format!("{}", set)) matches to_str().

implementation_plan.title: Equality and ordering comparisons
implementation_plan.goal: equal()/PartialEq compare (support, intervals) structurally; is_strict_subset_of/is_subset_of/is_disjoint faithfully reproduce the C quirk-behaviors (not true subset/disjoint tests).
steps_part_a: Implement InversionList::equal(other): compare self.support == other.support && self.intervals == other.intervals.
Implement impl PartialEq for InversionList::eq to call the same logic as equal (or vice versa); Eq is a marker (already declared).
Implement InversionList::is_strict_subset_of(other): self.support < other.support && exists a member of other in 0..self's last interval upper bound (port the C boundary-probe verbatim).
Implement InversionList::is_subset_of(other): self.equal(other) || self.is_strict_subset_of(other).
Implement InversionList::is_disjoint(other): !self.equal(other) (faithful alias of not_equal, per the C bug).
steps_part_b: Remove #[ignore] from test_equals: assert equal()/== for identical and differently-shaped sets; assert is_strict_subset_of/is_subset_of/is_disjoint reproduce the exact (non-standard) C outcomes on constructed pairs designed to expose the quirk (e.g. smaller-support set with no true subset relation).

implementation_plan.title: Value iterator
implementation_plan.goal: InversionListIterator visits every member value ascending exactly once, exhausting correctly (including on an empty set).
steps_part_a: Implement InversionListIterator::new(list): interval_index = 0, current_value = list.intervals.get(0).map(|(lo,_)| *lo).unwrap_or(0).

Implement impl Iterator for InversionListIterator::next: if interval_index is past the last interval, return None; otherwise yield current_value, advance current_value, and move to interval_index+1 once current_value reaches the current interval's upper bound.
steps_part_b: Remove #[ignore] from test_iterator: assert iterating a multi-interval set yields all members ascending exactly once; assert iterating an empty set yields no items.

implementation_plan.title: Couple (range) iterator
implementation_plan.goal: InversionListCoupleIterator visits every (inf, sup) interval exactly once in order, exhausting correctly (including on an empty set).
steps_part_a: Implement InversionListCoupleIterator::new(list): couple_index = 0.
Implement impl Iterator for InversionListCoupleIterator::next: if couple_index >= list.intervals.len(), return None; else return list.intervals[couple_index], increment couple_index.
steps_part_b: Remove #[ignore] from test_couple_iterator: assert iterating a multi-interval set yields each (inf,sup) tuple in interval order exactly once; assert an empty set yields no items.

implementation_plan.title: Set algebra operations
implementation_plan.goal: complement/union/intersection/difference/symmetric_difference match the C brute-force/two-pointer semantics exactly, bugs included (e.g. difference's fixed-min quirk), with capacity = max(self.capacity, other.capacity) for binary ops.
implementation_plan.gate_cmd: cargo test --lib -- test_complement test_union test_intersection test_difference
steps_part_a: Implement InversionList::complement: reproduce the C boundary add/drop logic for whether 0/capacity are boundary members; support becomes capacity - support.

Implement InversionList::union(other): brute-force scan over 0..max(self,other bounds) collecting values where self.contains(v) || other.contains(v), coalesce via the same logic as new(); capacity = max(self.capacity, other.capacity).
Implement InversionList::intersection(other): mirror the C two-pointer/overlap walk (or membership-scan restricted to overlap) producing coalesced intervals for values in both sets.

Implement InversionList::difference(other): mirror the C two-pointer walk collecting values in self but not other, faithfully reproducing the fixed-min (`set1`'s own first boundary rather than max(self_min, other_min)) quirk noted in analysis.md.
Implement InversionList::symmetric_difference(other): self.union(other).difference(&self.intersection(other)), matching the C composition exactly.
steps_part_b: Remove #[ignore] from test_complement: assert complement() boundary cases -- starts at 0, ends at capacity, neither, both -- and support == capacity - support.
Remove #[ignore] from test_union: assert union() over overlapping/disjoint/touching/empty operand pairs.
Remove #[ignore] from test_intersection: assert intersection() over overlapping/disjoint/touching/empty operand pairs.
Remove #[ignore] from test_difference: assert difference() over overlapping/disjoint/touching/empty operand pairs, including a case that exposes the fixed-min quirk faithfully.
